skill.name: typography
skill.description: Typography guidance for choosing distinctive fonts, pairing typefaces, and using strong weight and size contrast.
skill.summary: Design stronger typography with distinctive fonts and clear visual contrast.
skill.author: Crossbill-Highlights

security_audit.summary: The static system reconnaissance finding is a false positive caused by wording about design quality in SKILL.md. No prompt injection, data exfiltration intent, command execution, network abuse, or filesystem abuse was found in the reviewed file.

static_findings.snippet: Typography instantly signals quality. Avoid using boring, generic fonts.

finding_verdicts.reason: Line 5 gives typography advice about perceived design quality. It does not request system information, environment details, files, commands, or reconnaissance activity.

content.value_statement: Generic typography can make a product feel unfinished. This skill helps Claude, Codex, and Claude Code choose stronger fonts, pairings, weights, and size contrast.
actual_capabilities: Recommends distinctive font families for code, editorial, technical, and expressive interfaces.
Guides font pairing through strong contrast between display, serif, sans, and monospace styles.
Encourages decisive use of one primary distinctive typeface across a design.
Suggests larger weight and size differences to improve visual hierarchy.
Advises loading selected typefaces from Google Fonts when suitable.
limitations: It does not audit font licensing or commercial usage rights.
It does not measure accessibility, readability, or language coverage automatically.
It does not provide complete brand systems or full design specifications.
It depends on the model to apply the guidance in the current design context.

use_cases.title: Refresh Product Typography
use_cases.description: Improve a web app or landing page that feels generic because of default font choices.

use_cases.title: Strengthen Interface Hierarchy
use_cases.description: Select stronger weights and size jumps for headings, labels, and supporting text.

use_cases.title: Choose Brand Font Direction
use_cases.description: Explore font pairings that match editorial, technical, code-focused, or distinctive brand goals.

prompt_templates.title: Pick a Better Font
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this interface and recommend one distinctive font family that fits the product tone. Explain why it improves the design.

prompt_templates.title: Create Font Pairings
prompt_templates.prompt: Suggest three font pairings for this design. Include one display and monospace option, one serif and geometric sans option, and one variable font option.

prompt_templates.title: Improve Visual Hierarchy
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit the typography scale, weights, and contrast in this screen. Recommend specific size and weight changes for headings, labels, and body text.

prompt_templates.title: Define Typography Direction
prompt_templates.prompt: Create a typography direction for this product. Include primary font choice, secondary pairing, weight range, size contrast, and Google Fonts loading guidance.

output_examples.input: A developer tool uses default system fonts and weak heading contrast.
output_examples.output: Use JetBrains Mono for code surfaces and Space Grotesk for headings. Pair 200-weight section labels with 800-weight headings for stronger hierarchy.

output_examples.input: An editorial page needs a more refined reading experience.
output_examples.output: Use Playfair Display for large titles and Source Sans 3 for body copy. Keep the title scale much larger than paragraph text.

output_examples.input: A technical dashboard needs a less generic visual identity.
output_examples.output: Use the IBM Plex family across sans and mono styles. Apply one distinctive type system consistently instead of mixing many unrelated fonts.

best_practices: Choose one distinctive primary font and use it consistently across the experience.
Use strong contrast between type categories, weights, and sizes to create hierarchy.
Test font choices in real interface states before finalizing the design.
anti_patterns: Using default system fonts when the product needs a distinctive visual identity.
Making small weight changes that do not create clear hierarchy.
Combining many expressive fonts without a clear role for each typeface.

faq.question: What does this skill help with?
faq.answer: It helps choose stronger fonts, pairings, weights, and size contrast for digital product typography.

faq.question: Can it choose production-ready font files?
faq.answer: It can suggest font families, but you must confirm licensing, performance, and language coverage.

faq.question: Does it work with Claude and Codex?
faq.answer: Yes. The report lists support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is this a full design system skill?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on typography choices and hierarchy, not complete tokens or component specifications.

faq.question: Can it improve an existing interface?
faq.answer: Yes. Provide the current design context and ask for font, weight, and size recommendations.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: No. The skill contains guidance only and does not include scripts or network code.
